one_liner: Issue tracking and project management platform for software teams

evidence.claim: Linear API supports both personal API keys and OAuth2 authentication
evidence.quote: The Linear API supports personal API keys and OAuth2 authentication.

evidence.claim: OAuth2 is documented with self-serve app creation in workspace settings
evidence.quote: Linear supports OAuth2 authentication, which is recommended if you’re building applications to integrate with Linear.

evidence.claim: Public API is GraphQL and covers the full product
evidence.quote: Linear’s public API is built using GraphQL. It’s the same API we use internally for developing our applications.

evidence.claim: API/webhooks cover many entity types, indicating broad surface
evidence.quote: Our webhooks support data change events for Issues, Comments, Issue attachments, Documents, Emoji reactions, Projects, Project updates, Cycles, Labels, Users and Issue SLAs.

evidence.claim: Linear ships an official MCP server documented on its own docs site
evidence.quote: Our MCP server uses Streamable HTTP as the primary transport, accessible at the following address.

notes: Official MCP server uses Streamable HTTP with OAuth 2.1 and dynamic client registration. All OAuth2 apps were migrated to a new refresh token system on April 1, 2026. Agent integrations use OAuth2 with actor=app and agent-specific scopes like app:assignable and app:mentionable. Admins can disable member API key creation (Settings > Administration > API), but admins always can create keys; webhook and OAuth app management requires admin permissions.
